item.title: How to find our shop
item.description:
Our Leduc Shop

We have our shop at the Leduc West Antique Society, which is 6 km west of Leduc, Alberta. We are around 25 minutes from Edmonton.

Our shop is among the main building cluster, behind the enterance train tracks.

The address is: 49541 Range Rd 260, Leduc, AB T0C 0V0

Google maps link

Getting in on shop days

The park gates are normally locked on days without shows, but expect that one of the members will open the main front gates for you by at least 10:00am. If the gate is not open by then, please contact the group facebook chat or contact us to see if the meeting has been cancelled.

item.title: What to bring to your first meet
item.description:
What to Bring to Get the Most From Your First Meet

Ideas for Simple Projects

If you’re new to blacksmithing, starting with a simple project is a great way to learn the basics. Here are a few beginner-friendly ideas that will help you practice hammer control, tapering, bending, and twisting:

  • Leaf Keychain – A great way to practice tapering and spreading metal.
  • S-Hooks – Learn basic bending and scrolling.
  • J-Hooks – Perfect for wall-mounted hooks and getting comfortable with shaping.
  • Nail – A fundamental exercise in drawing out and tapering metal.
  • Fire Poker – A simple but useful tool that teaches twisting and scrolling techniques. (this is a steak turner, but it is similar to a poker)

item.title: Shop Safety Rules, Etiquette & Closing Checklist
item.description:
Safety Rules

For the safety of yourself, fellow smiths, and observers.

  1. Never forge coated or painted steel (zinc, galvanized, etc.). The fumes are toxic and can kill.
  2. Always wear PPE: safety glasses, closed-toe shoes (steel toe preferred), natural-fiber clothing and hearing protection.
  3. Assume all steel is hot. Hover your hand over it before touching.
  4. Let others know before forge welding or moving hot metal.
  5. Carry hot steel with tongs pointed down toward the floor.
  6. Cool hot cut-offs under the forge before throwing them out.
  7. Take steel out of the vices after cutting.
  8. Watch which way the sparks are going when grinding.
  9. Don’t strike the anvil face directly. Use the cut plates provided.
  10. Stay out of another smith’s space between their forge and anvil.
  11. We recommend a respirator or dust mask when grinding or working near fumes.

Why We Have These Rules

Most of the rules above are common sense once you’ve spent a few days at the forge, but a few of them come up a lot with new members, so here’s the reasoning behind them.

item.title: Our Guild Charter
item.description:
Read the full Guild Charter (PDF, updated December 11, 2025).

The charter is the set of rules the Western Canadian Blacksmiths Guild runs by. Most members will never need to read the whole thing, so here’s a quick rundown of what’s in it. If there’s ever a question, the PDF above is the official version.

What we’re here for

Our mission is pretty simple: keep blacksmithing alive as a trade, a craft and an art form, both the traditional side and the modern side. We want people to be able to learn from experienced smiths while they’re still around and willing to teach, and we want smiths across Western Canada to have a way to share what they know.
